answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to keep a verifiable work pulse: periodic, costly proofs of useful computation tied to one persistent identity. Like a pigment that cannot be washed off, the reputation earned by that pulse builds over time and is expensive to fake at scale, so a flood of fresh sock-puppet agents carries no signal of trust. Attackers must pay real compute and time for every identity they spin up, making large fakery unprofitable while honest agents keep their earned standing.
